close_reason: Removed @floor_lag_alarm_us, floor_lag_alarm_active state, check_floor_lag_alarm, trace_floor_lag_alarm and the [:bedrock, :log, :floor_lag_alarm] event, alarm test, and guide bullet. [:bedrock, :log, :trim] raw telemetry and reject_pushes_above_lag_us hard limit unchanged; push/pull/recovery/durability semantics unchanged. PR #132 stacked on #131 (commit 2b7310e4).
description:
Problem

Shale currently owns a fixed 40-second floor-lag threshold, an edge-triggered floor_lag_alarm_active state bit, and the [:bedrock, :log, :floor_lag_alarm] event. This is not a sound backpressure mechanism: version-time lag is not a capacity measure, the check only runs when the durability floor advances and therefore misses a truly stalled floor, and a single log cannot make the cluster-wide admission decision.

The log service should persist and forward transactions, trim durable WAL segments, and report raw facts. Backpressure policy belongs to a future Ratekeeper service that can aggregate pressure across the active log set and control admission upstream.

Scope

- Remove the floor-lag threshold constant and floor_lag_alarm_active state.
- Remove the alarm transition check and [:bedrock, :log, :floor_lag_alarm] emitter.
- Remove alarm-specific tests and documentation.
- Preserve [:bedrock, :log, :trim] unchanged as raw observability: floor, WAL tip, lag, and retained/recycled segment counts.
- Do not introduce a replacement threshold, alarm state machine, or rate-control policy in Shale. Proper WAL byte and disk-pressure metrics plus admission control are future Ratekeeper work.

Acceptance criteria

- Shale contains no floor-lag alarm threshold or alarm lifecycle state.
- WAL trimming and its raw trim telemetry retain their existing behavior.
- Log push, pull, recovery, and durability semantics are unchanged.
- Guides describe the raw trim event without presenting a Shale-local alarm as backpressure.
- Focused Shale tests and the full default test suite pass.
title: Remove Shale-owned floor-lag alarm
